samples.summary: The conditional GoogleStrategy provider factory — the change's whole "Google is optional, and registered only after dotenv has run" contract — has no test anywhere
samples.evidence: `googleStrategyProvider` (auth.module.ts:55-60) is the piece whose own doc comment records a real prior outage: evaluated at module scope it read `process.env` before `ConfigModule.forRoot()`, so `/auth/providers` and `GoogleAuthGuard` said "configured" while passport had no `google` strategy and every Google login died with `Unknown authentication strategy "google"`. There is no `auth.module.spec.ts` (Glob `packages/backend/src/auth/*.ts` shows every spec; none covers the module), and grepping `AuthModule|googleStrategyProvider` across packages/backend finds only source and README hits. A `Test.createTestingModule({ imports: [AuthModule] })` assertion — strategy present with the vars set via `process.env` after import, absent without — is the one thing that would catch the regression, and nothing asserts it. Also untested: `googleAuthPartiallyConfigured()`/`missingGoogleAuthVars()` feeding the boot warning (auth.module.ts:97-105).

samples.summary: The GitHub web-flow state-refusal tests never assert `findOrCreateUser` was not called, so the diff's move of the upsert behind the state check is untested on the GitHub side
samples.evidence: The diff's stated property is "Checked *before* the user is upserted, so a refused callback leaves no row (and no workspace) behind" (auth.controller.ts:319). The Google suite asserts it (auth.controller.spec.ts, `expect(userService.findOrCreateUser).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` in the `refuses %s` it.each), but the pre-existing GitHub web-flow cases at auth.controller.spec.ts:430-486 only assert `res.redirect` and `res.cookie`. Reverting the GitHub handler to the old order (upsert first, state check second) would leave every GitHub test green while forged/expired callbacks again create user rows and workspaces. Same for the CLI-branch refusal tests at lines 314-365.

samples.summary: `consumeWebOAuthState` is never covered by a test asserting the state cookie is cleared on a MISMATCH (single-use on failure); only the success path is asserted
samples.evidence: web-oauth-login.ts:66-71 clears the cookie before comparing, documented as "cleared whether or not it matches, so a failed login leaves nothing behind to replay". There is no `web-oauth-login.spec.ts` (Glob of packages/backend/src/auth shows none), and the refusal tests in auth.controller.spec.ts (GitHub lines 430-486, Google `refuses %s` block) assert only `redirect` and `cookie`, never `clearCookie`. Moving the `clearCookie` after the match check would pass the whole suite while leaving a replayable state cookie behind.

samples.summary: No test covers `finishWebLogin`'s returnTo round trip — the Google callback never asserts a stored returnTo cookie is honoured, cleared and re-validated
samples.evidence: `finishWebLogin` (auth.controller.ts:355-369) reads the `returnTo` cookie, clears it and re-validates through `safeReturnPath`. Grepping `returnTo|loginReturnCookieName` across `packages/backend/src/auth/*.spec.ts` returns hits only in google-auth.guard.spec.ts (the WRITE side, at the start route). No controller test supplies a `loginReturnCookieName()` cookie, so the read side — including the re-validation that is described as "the actual guard" against an attacker-written cookie — is exercised by nothing for either provider.

samples.summary: The workspace-slug retry loop (P2002 race) and its attempt cap are never exercised: every test takes the attempt-0 path
samples.evidence: `createUserWithWorkspace` catches `isSlugConflict(error)` and retries up to `SLUG_ATTEMPTS`. In user.service.spec.ts the colliding-name test hits `freeSlug` attempt 0, which finds the base taken via `findUnique` and returns a random-suffixed slug — the workspace insert then succeeds, so the `catch` branch, `isSlugConflict`, the `attempt >= SLUG_ATTEMPTS` rethrow and the post-rollback re-creation of the user row never run. A broken `isSlugConflict` (e.g. wrong `meta.target` shape) would turn a race into a hard 500 that no test detects. The fake prisma already supports it — a `workspace.create` that rejects with P2002 once would cover it.

samples.summary: `loginRefusalMessage`'s unknown-code sanitisation is untested, and the refusal test does not assert the exit code
samples.evidence: login-callback.test.ts only drives `?error=unverified_email` (lines 96-130), which hits the known-code branch. The fallback at login.ts:621 — reduce anything not matching `/^[a-z0-9_]{1,40}$/` to `unknown` — has no test, and neither does the `no_email`/`email_conflict` wording. Note the lookup is a plain object literal, so `?error=constructor` returns a truthy function and would be interpolated into the message (`Sign-in was refused: function Object() {...}`) — exactly the prototype-chain hazard `login-form.tsx` avoids by using a `Map`, and no test would notice. The refusal test also asserts only the message regex, never `EXIT_USER_ERROR` on the thrown `LoginError`.

samples.summary: `fetchAuthProviders`'s non-OK-response fallback is untested — the helper takes an `ok` flag that no test ever passes as false
samples.evidence: `stubProviders(body, ok = true)` is declared with an `ok` parameter, but every call site in the diff omits it, so `if (!res.ok) return fallback;` in api/auth.ts is dead in the suite. The `github: body.github !== false` parsing is likewise never exercised with a missing/false field. The only failure path covered is the rejected-promise one. A 500 from `/auth/providers` returning an HTML error body would take the `res.json()` path in a regression and nothing would catch it.

samples.summary: GitHub's `isFlagSet` string-"true" branch is untested, unlike the identical Google helper
samples.evidence: github.strategy.ts:29 accepts the string `"true"` for `verified`/`primary`, but the new `GitHubStrategy verified email` suite only feeds booleans (`verified: true`/`false`/absent). The Google side tests the string form explicitly (google.strategy.spec.ts `accepts %s as verification`). If GitHub ever returns the string shape the behaviour is unproven either way.

samples.summary: `oauthRefusal` is never tested with an error code outside the closed vocabulary
samples.evidence: `oauthRefusal` deliberately ignores unknown `error` strings, after which `resolveOAuthUser` calls `findOrCreateUser` with `profile.username!`/`profile.email!` both undefined. No test in auth.controller.spec.ts passes `req.user = { error: 'something_else' }`, so what happens on an unrecognised refusal (a 500 vs a redirect) is unspecified by the suite.

verdict.reason: The conditional provider factory at packages/backend/src/auth/auth.module.ts:55-60 and the partial-config boot warning at auth.module.ts:97-105 exist as described, and nothing in the repository tests them. A repo-wide grep for `AuthModule` returns only src modules (app/document/template/folder) plus README/design docs — no test file imports AuthModule, so no test ever instantiates the injector that decides whether GoogleStrategy is constructed and registered with passport. `googleStrategyProvider` appears only at auth.module.ts:55 and :85. `googleAuthPartiallyConfigured`/`missingGoogleAuthVars` (oauth-providers.ts:47-55) are referenced only by auth.module.ts:98-100; there is no oauth-providers.spec.ts. I searched beyond the reviewer's paths: the entire packages/backend/test/ e2e suite (several specs do boot AppModule, which pulls in AuthModule, but a grep for `google` across that directory yields a single unrelated BigQuery comment at authenticated-http.e2e-spec.ts:445, and none assert strategy presence/absence or the warning), plus repo-wide greps for `Unknown authentication strategy|strategies|auth/google` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`. The adjacent specs that do exist test different units by direct construction: google-auth.guard.spec.ts (404 path via googleAuthConfigured), auth.controller.spec.ts:721-747 (GET /auth/providers env flipping), google.strategy.spec.ts (validate/authenticate) — none goes through the module, so none can catch the documented regression where the strategy is absent while /auth/providers and the guard say "configured". Major: an undetected failure here ships either a dead Google login (Unknown authentication strategy "google") or a boot failure for installs without Google credentials.
